quests.sentence: She will finish the presentation tomorrow.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will finish uses the base verb finish after will, with tomorrow (future time) closing the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Will sits right after the subject, before the base form of the verb.

quests.sentence: They will attend the conference.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will attend keeps attend in base form after the plural subject They, with the conference as the object.
quests.nativeTip: The base verb never changes form after will, no matter the subject.

quests.sentence: I will help you with this.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will help precedes you (indirect object) and with this (extra detail), keeping the base verb right after will.
quests.nativeTip: Will stays in the same spot even with a double object after the verb.

quests.sentence: He won't finish on time.
quests.ruleExplanation: Won't replaces will not before finish (base form), with on time closing the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Won't fuses will and not into one word, still followed by the base verb.

quests.sentence: They won't accept the offer.
quests.ruleExplanation: Won't precedes accept (base form), with the offer as the object.
quests.nativeTip: The same contraction sits before the base verb, regardless of subject.

quests.sentence: She won't miss the deadline.
quests.ruleExplanation: Won't precedes miss (base form), with the deadline as the object.
quests.nativeTip: Won't still comes right before the base verb, keeping the negative and modal fused.

quests.sentence: Will she join us later?
quests.ruleExplanation: Will moves ahead of she to form the question, with join us later following in normal order.
quests.nativeTip: Move will to the front of the sentence, ahead of the subject, to form the question.

quests.sentence: Will they extend the deadline?
quests.ruleExplanation: Will leads the question before they, followed by extend the deadline.
quests.nativeTip: Will inverts with the subject the same way for any subject type.

quests.sentence: Will the store deliver it today?
quests.ruleExplanation: Will opens the question before the store, followed by deliver it today.
quests.nativeTip: Will still opens the question, with the base verb and object following the subject.

quests.sentence: She is going to start a new job.
quests.ruleExplanation: Is going to start shows a planned intention, with going to sitting between is and the base verb start.
quests.nativeTip: Going to sits between is/am/are and the base verb, showing a plan already decided.

quests.sentence: They are going to renovate the kitchen.
quests.ruleExplanation: Are going to renovate follows the same pattern, showing They already have a plan to renovate the kitchen.
quests.nativeTip: The same going to pattern applies with are, for a plural subject.

quests.sentence: I am going to visit my grandparents.
quests.ruleExplanation: Am going to visit follows I, showing a decided plan, with my grandparents as the object.
quests.nativeTip: I pairs with am, then going to, then the base verb, same as with present continuous.

quests.sentence: He is not going to attend the party.
quests.ruleExplanation: Not sits between is and going to, showing He has decided against attending the party.
quests.nativeTip: Not slots in between is/are and going to, the same spot it takes with present continuous.

quests.sentence: They aren't going to renew the lease.
quests.ruleExplanation: Aren't replaces are not right before going to renew, showing a decided plan not to renew the lease.
quests.nativeTip: Aren't fuses are and not, staying right before going to.

quests.sentence: She isn't going to change her plans.
quests.ruleExplanation: Isn't precedes going to change, showing She has firmly decided not to change her plans.
quests.nativeTip: Isn't works the same way, fusing is and not before going to.

quests.sentence: Is she going to accept the offer?
quests.ruleExplanation: Is moves ahead of she to form the question, with going to accept the offer following in order.
quests.nativeTip: Move is to the front, ahead of the subject, to ask about a plan.

quests.sentence: Are they going to sell the house?
quests.ruleExplanation: Are leads the question before they, followed by going to sell the house.
quests.nativeTip: Are inverts with the subject the same way, asking about a plural subject's plan.

quests.sentence: Are you going to apply for the position?
quests.ruleExplanation: Are opens the question before you, and going to apply for the position follows, with for the position extending the object.
quests.nativeTip: The same question pattern holds even with a longer prepositional phrase at the end.

quests.sentence: It is going to rain because of those dark clouds.
quests.ruleExplanation: Going to rain is used because those dark clouds are visible evidence right now — going to is for predictions based on something you can already see.
quests.nativeTip: Use going to when there's visible evidence right now pointing to what will happen.

quests.sentence: I will carry that heavy box for you.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will carry expresses a decision made spontaneously, right at the moment of offering — the classic use of will, unlike a pre-made plan with going to.
quests.nativeTip: Use will for a decision made on the spot, right at the moment of speaking.

quests.sentence: I promise I will call you tonight.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will call expresses a promise here, reinforced by I promise — another core use of will, distinct from a fixed plan or a visible prediction.
quests.nativeTip: Will also expresses a promise, a personal commitment about the future.

quests.conceptTitle: Future Time Clauses (Present Tense for Future Meaning)
quests.sentence: She will call you when she arrives.
quests.ruleExplanation: When she arrives uses the present tense arrives to refer to a future event, paired with will call in the main clause.
quests.nativeTip: In a future time clause with when, use the present tense, even though the meaning is future.

quests.conceptTitle: Future Time Clauses (Present Tense for Future Meaning)
quests.sentence: They will start the meeting as soon as everyone arrives.
quests.ruleExplanation: As soon as everyone arrives uses present tense arrives for a future event, while will start carries the future meaning in the main clause.
quests.nativeTip: As soon as works the same way — present tense in the time clause, will in the main clause.

quests.conceptTitle: Future Time Clauses (Present Tense for Future Meaning)
quests.sentence: He will send the invoice before he leaves.
quests.ruleExplanation: Before he leaves uses present tense leaves for a future event, while will send carries the future meaning in the main clause.
quests.nativeTip: Before also takes the present tense in a future time clause, not will.

quests.sentence: What will you do after graduation?
quests.ruleExplanation: What opens the question, will follows, you is the subject, and do after graduation completes it.
quests.nativeTip: The question word leads, then will, then the subject, then the base verb.

quests.sentence: Where are they going to stay?
quests.ruleExplanation: Where leads the question, are follows, they is the subject, and going to stay completes the plan-based question.
quests.nativeTip: Where comes first, then are, then the subject, then going to plus the base verb.

quests.sentence: When will the new policy take effect?
quests.ruleExplanation: When leads the question, will follows, the new policy is the subject, and take effect completes it.
quests.nativeTip: When still opens the question, followed by will, the subject, and the base verb with its object.

quests.sentence: She is going to present her findings when the workshop begins.
quests.ruleExplanation: Is going to present states the plan, and when the workshop begins (present tense, future meaning) names the future time clause.
quests.nativeTip: Combine going to for a plan with a future time clause using present tense.

quests.sentence: I will send you the documents as soon as I finish.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will send precedes you (indirect object) and the documents (direct object), followed by as soon as I finish (present tense, future meaning).
quests.nativeTip: Combine will with a double object and an as-soon-as time clause in present tense.

quests.sentence: They won't announce the results until their review is complete.
quests.ruleExplanation: Won't announce is the negative future action, and until their review is complete uses present tense is for a future condition.
quests.nativeTip: Combine won't with an until-clause that also uses present tense for future meaning.
